Svirfneblin

Humanoid (Gnome) · minor threat

Humanoid (Gnome) · 1 hex · SM -2 Svirfneblin [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: humanoid folk and their sub-races; answers Svirfneblin (SRD 5.1); Svirfneblin (SRD 3.5)]

Deep gnomes: grey, wiry, and the most cautious folk under any mountain. Svirfneblin live between the dwarven holds and worse neighbours, and have survived it by never once being where anyone expected. Magic thrown at one tends to fail outright, and against stone at three paces they are effectively not there.

Notes

  • GCS ancestry draft: gcs/svirfneblin.gct
  • Independent build total: 64 points of racial traits plus 34 points of racial skills.
  • Answers the SRD heading(s): Svirfneblin (SRD 5.1); Svirfneblin (SRD 3.5). Only the creature identity is taken from the SRD; the GURPS statistics, ratings and prose are this project's own work and reproduce no SRD text.
  • Typical Stats, damage and ratings are derived from the racial template, not authored beside it, so the sheet and the stat block cannot disagree.
  • Body mass used to scale this build: 25 kg. ST, Size Modifier and DR are checked against it; see the gurps-animal-sanity-check skill for the bands.
  • Movement: ground Move 4 (primary). The published Move is the primary medium's cruising Move; sprint figures are stated here and not folded into it.
  • Treasure and grappling are not authored for this batch and ship as explicit nulls; `lair` carries a short habitat note, because where a wandering animal dens is an encounter fact rather than a loot one.
  • About 0.9 m standing, which is the SM -2 row.
  • ST 8 from the gnome stock: a small frame that has spent its life underground and is wiry rather than strong.
  • Magic Resistance 3 is the highest in this batch and is the reason the creature has survived where it lives.
  • Silence 3 on top of a very high Stealth, and the same distinction as the forest gnome: the advantage is what nothing hears, the skill is what nothing sees.
  • The camouflage and non-detection a svirfneblin can call are not built as traits. Both come and go rather than being what it is, and the vocabulary prices what a creature is.
